content_units: 90-Minute Dinner Party Flow

A smooth dinner party arc works best when it starts warm and welcoming, settles into intimate conversation, then gently lifts into brighter groove by dessert or late glasses. From your 15 tracks, I’d cut 3 that disrupt that flow most and sequence the remaining 12 for a classy, cohesive rise in energy.
Sequenced Playlist and Energy Arc
Artist   Track   Why it sits here
1   Norah Jones   Don’t Know Why   Soft, familiar opener; instantly puts the room at ease.
2   Rhye   Open   Keeps the intimacy high with a sensual, low-volume glide.
3   Al Green   Let’s Stay Together   Warm soul lift; still elegant, but more social and inviting.
4   Sade   Smooth Operator   Sophisticated lounge momentum; perfect early-dinner mood.
5   Khruangbin   Friday Morning   Airy groove transition that keeps conversation front and center.
6   Erykah Badu   On & On   Deepens the pocket with relaxed neo-soul texture.
7   Michael Kiwanuka   Cold Little Heart   Expands the room emotionally; a richer mid-set centerpiece.
8   Daft Punk   Something About Us   Smooth modern comedown from the drama into sleek romance.
9   SAULT   Wildfires   Cool, understated pulse; thoughtful but still rhythmically grounded.
10   Bill Withers   Lovely Day   Lightens everything; this is where the room starts smiling wider.
11   Amy Winehouse   Valerie   Recognizable, upbeat sing-along energy without going full dancefloor.
12   Parcels   Tieduprightnow   Chic, buoyant closer that leaves the party lifted and loose.
Why These 3 Were Cut
1.   Jungle – Busy Earnin’
- Great track, but it pushes too hard and too early toward party-mode.
- Its punchier funk energy can make the set feel less dinner-friendly and more pre-club.
2.   Thundercat – Them Changes
- Excellent song, but its bounce and tonal quirkiness pull attention away from the smooth, elegant flow.
- It feels more like a clever left turn than a seamless dinner transition.
3.   Phoenix – Lisztomania
- Big indie-pop release and brighter edge than the rest of the set.
- It can work at the very end, but compared with Parcels it feels less silky and more shouty for this brief.
How the Night Progresses
Welcome Pour: soft, intimate, polished
-   Norah Jones → Rhye → Al Green
- This first stretch is low-pressure and warm.
- Guests can arrive, settle in, and talk without competing with the music.
Main Course: sophisticated groove
-   Sade → Khruangbin → Erykah Badu → Michael Kiwanuka
- This is the heart of the playlist.
- It adds character, depth, and a little emotional richness while staying cool and conversational.
Late Dinner Glow: smoother pulse, brighter mood
-   Daft Punk → SAULT → Bill Withers
- The set becomes more rhythmic and lightly more modern.
- Energy rises, but still feels tasteful and relaxed.
Dessert and Last Glass: upbeat but not rowdy
-   Amy Winehouse → Parcels
- Familiarity and motion increase just enough to feel celebratory.
- You end with momentum, not a peak that overwhelms the room.
Quick Swap Option
If you want a slightly more playful finish:
- Replace   SAULT – Wildfires   with   Phoenix – Lisztomania
- Keep it at position 12 instead of Parcels for a more extroverted closer
